reason: Glucose and oxygen are the fuel inputs described for making usable energy, and the cell has the transporter for sugar.
expectation: The cell should take in fuel for the energy-making process.

effect: The cell forms the muscle fibre scaffold with the fibre structures; fuel must be handled through another combination.
reaction: The automatic combination clarified the starting point, though the fuel attempt was a guess.
reason: Mitochondria are associated with making usable energy from glucose and oxygen.
expectation: This should begin the process of making ATP.

effect: Glucose and oxygen fuelled the mitochondria; ADP and phosphate now look like the next inputs for making ATP.
reaction: The picture clarified that glucose is first split in the cell fluid.
reason: ADP and phosphate are the available components for making ATP.
expectation: The fuelled mitochondria should produce ATP from ADP and phosphate.

effect: The fuelled mitochondria produced an ATP supply that can support the fibre’s pulling machinery.
reaction: The picture makes the recycling of ADP and phosphate clear.
reason: Thin and thick filaments appear to be the complementary parts of the pulling machinery.
expectation: The filaments should form a contractile unit that can be fitted into the muscle fibre.

effect: The thin and thick filaments form sliding filament units that appear ready to fit into the muscle fibre.
reaction: The overlapping arrangement makes the connection between the two filament types clearer.
reason: The muscle fibre scaffold has spaces for contractile units, and these units look like the intended fit.
expectation: The sliding filament units should become part of the muscle fibre.

effect: The sliding filament units are now installed in the muscle fibre; it still needs a signal and energy to pull and relax.
reaction: The scaffold and filament units fit together as expected.
reason: The calcium pulse is described as spreading around the fibre’s filaments, so it looks like the trigger for a pull.
expectation: The calcium signal should activate the fibre’s pulling machinery.

effect: The fibre needs ATP before the calcium signal can act; it is now ATP-ready.
reaction: The ATP step clarified that myosin must release and reset before pulling.
reason: The calcium signal remains the apparent trigger for the prepared filaments.
expectation: Calcium should activate the fibre’s pulling machinery.

effect: Calcium exposed grip sites and the fibre shortened as its filaments slid past each other; the remaining goal is relaxation.
reaction: The distinction between the fibre shortening and the filaments sliding was clear and interesting.
reason: The calcium-pumping membranes appear to remove the calcium signal so the fibre can relax.
expectation: Calcium will be pumped back into storage, allowing the fibre to relax and prepare for another pull.

effect: Calcium pumps use ATP to return calcium to storage, covering the grip sites and stopping the pull; the fibre relaxes under an outside pull and is ready to respond again.
reaction: It was interesting that relaxation also requires cellular work.

mostWorthwhile.text: Activating the ATP-ready fibre was most worthwhile because the result connected calcium, myosin and sliding filaments to the fibre shortening. The picture description clearly distinguished filament sliding from the filaments themselves shortening.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the filaments to the fibre was predictable, and its result added little explanation beyond showing them packed together. It was still a clear construction step.

surprise.text: I was surprised that ATP had to be added before the calcium signal could act. The picture description showed ATP helping myosin release and reset.

arbitrary.text: The initial attempt to combine the cell with fuel was a reasonable guess from the titles, but the automatic move to the fibre scaffold did not explain why fuel could not be used there. The later mitochondria result made the intended route clearer.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the sequence connected fuel, ATP, contraction and relaxation in a way that made me curious how a working fibre becomes part of a larger body system. The picture descriptions were helpful, though their effectiveness as finished illustrations remains untested.
